title: Meet the UK's New Prime Minister: Andy Burnham, the Dad Dancer!
summary: Who is Andy Burnham? He's about to be the UK's 59th prime minister, and he's not your typical politician. He's 56 years old, a huge Everton soccer fan, and he even danced to a song called "True Faith" at a big party! Some people call him a "dad dancer" because of his moves. But there's more to him than fun. Burnham used to be a cabinet minister, and he went to Cambridge University. He's also called "King of the North" because he's the mayor of Greater Manchester and people there really like him. But not everyone is happy. He became prime minister by pushing out the last one, Keir Starmer, in a kind of quiet revolt. Even people who are mad at him say he's a nice person. One old friend said, "He is a lovely bloke, but I just don't know if he is up to it." Being nice might not be enough to run a country. Burnham is also willing to be tough. He once got advice from Sir Alex Ferguson, the famous Manchester United soccer coach. Ferguson said if he were in charge, he'd tell people, "You're either with me, or you can go." Burnham's team says he might use that same tough style. Already, he's made a decision that upset some allies: allowing new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea, even though his energy secretary is against it. So, is Burnham a friendly dancer or a ruthless leader? Maybe he's both.
why_it_matters: This shows that leaders can be both fun and serious, but the important thing is making decisions that affect people's lives, like energy jobs or the environment.

background_read: Sir Alex Ferguson, a legendary soccer coach who led Manchester United to many titles, famously said 'You're either with me, or you can go,' a tough leadership style Burnham might use.
The North Sea is the body of water east of the UK; drilling there provides oil and gas but is controversial because burning these fuels contributes to climate change.
Article_Structure: WHO: Andy Burnham, the 59th UK prime minister, mayor of Greater Manchester, and an Everton fan known as 'King of the North' and a 'dad dancer'.
WHAT: He took power by pushing out Keir Starmer in a quiet revolt and brings a mix of friendly charm and a tough, 'you're with me or you go' attitude.
WHERE: In the United Kingdom, with roots in Manchester; the story includes his dance at a party and his decision about the North Sea.
WHY: To show he's a capable leader, even if being nice isn't enough, he's willing to make difficult choices like allowing oil and gas drilling.

perspectives.description: They call him 'King of the North' and love that he's a regular guy who dances and supports Everton; they believe he will fight for people outside London.
They question if a 'lovely bloke' can handle the tough job of prime minister, and some think he betrayed Keir Starmer unfairly.
They are angry about the new oil and gas drilling, which they say goes against promises to fight climate change and protect the planet.
